name: Viviscal

lead: Viviscal is a marine-protein supplement taken twice daily by men and women with thinning hair who want more density and thickness. Small placebo-controlled trials in women and in men with male pattern hair loss report more terminal hairs and less shedding.

Its marine complex is proposed to support the hair growth cycle, though human mechanistic evidence is limited. A 2023 JAMA Dermatology systematic review listed it among supplements with the highest-quality evidence of potential benefit, with a general caution about the field.

paras: It is taken as an oral supplement twice daily, with Extra Strength and Man versions. Trials were small and short, and users generally expect months of consistent use.
Trials report few or no adverse events, and a systematic review described supplement adverse effects as rare and mild. It is sold as a dietary supplement.

angle.text: Viviscal is taken by men and women with thinning hair who want more density and thickness. A marine protein complex is said to support follicle nutrition and the hair growth cycle. A few placebo-controlled trials report more terminal hairs, and a 2023 review is cautiously positive.

lead: Viviscal is a branded oral supplement built around a marine protein complex, marketed for thinning hair in women and men. Its formulations include Extra Strength and Man versions.[1][2][3]

Published placebo-controlled trials of Viviscal products, in women and in men with male pattern hair loss, report more terminal hairs and less shedding than placebo.[2][3] A 2023 JAMA Dermatology systematic review counted Viviscal among supplements with the highest-quality evidence of potential benefit in people without known deficiency, while advising cautious interpretation.[4]
infobox: Marine protein complex and other ingredients

paras: A 1992 double-blind study in 40 young men with hereditary androgenic alopecia compared ViviScal with a fish extract for six months; it reported a mean 38 percent increase in non-vellus hair with ViviScal versus 2 percent with the control, and clinical and histological improvement in 19 of 20 treated subjects.[5] Most participants had previously used 2 percent topical minoxidil.[5]

A 90-day randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of Viviscal Extra Strength in 60 women with self-perceived thinning hair reported a significant rise in terminal hair count versus placebo, less shedding, higher self-assessment and quality of life scores, and no adverse events.[2] A 6-month randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of Viviscal Man in men with male pattern hair loss reported significant increases in total and terminal hair density and lower hair-pull test results versus placebo.[3]

Registered studies cover women with self-perceived thinning hair, including extra-strength and professional-strength formulations.[6][7][8] A 2026 meta-analysis assessed commercial oral supplements for hair growth, and a review of nutraceuticals for androgenetic alopecia and a network meta-analysis cover the topic more broadly; reviews describe the supplement evidence as needing cautious interpretation.[9][10][11][4]

A 2023 review of marine-derived ingredients discusses their proposed effects on the hair cell cycle.[12] Evidence for these mechanisms in humans from Viviscal is not established in the sources cited here.
The trials above reported few or no adverse events, and the JAMA Dermatology review described supplement adverse effects as rare and mild.[2][4]
